title: Adobe import fidelity: diagnostics + bitmap fills in buzz-import-xfl
summary: Follow plan §4 (docs/OBJECT_SELECTION_SHADOW_UI_PLAN.md, "Large Adobe Animate imports") starting with its steps 1–2 and the media-resolution part of step 3. Make ImportReport carry structured, per-entry diagnostics so nothing is lost silently, add a source-vs-parsed inventory reconciliation, then replace the flat-grey bitmap-fill fallback with real decoded image fills (including fill matrices) wired into buzz-scene's ImageLibrary/Paint::image. Text/video/sound get explicit placeholders + report entries this round rather than silent drops.

steps.description: Extend ImportReport in crates/buzz-import-xfl/src/lib.rs: add a structured `issues` list (archive entry name, symbol path, layer/frame where known, reason) alongside the existing deduped `unsupported` strings; convert the tracing::warn at line ~225 (skipped library entry) and every note_unsupported call site to record location. Keep unsupported/is_complete behavior for backward compat.
steps.verification: cargo test -p buzz-import-xfl passes; existing tests a_library_entry_that_will_not_decode_is_skipped_not_fatal and unsupported_features_are_reported still pass; add one test asserting the skipped-entry issue carries its entry name.

steps.description: Add source inventory reconciliation (plan step 1): count archive entries vs parsed library definitions/instances/layers in ImportReport (new fields: entries_total, symbols_parsed, instances_resolved, unresolved_refs), computed during import; expose them for app-level display. Never mark a partial import complete when counts don't reconcile.
steps.verification: cargo test -p buzz-import-xfl; new test on MINIMAL_DOCUMENT asserting counts match and a tampered fixture (extra library entry with bad XML) shows entries_total > symbols_parsed.

steps.description: Implement real bitmap fills: in the style-table parser (line ~1513 'BitmapFill' branch), resolve DOMBitmapFill to the decoded asset from self.bitmaps and emit buzz-scene Paint::image(ImageFill) with the fill matrix applied (map XFL transform matrix onto ImageFill/shape placement); drop the flat-grey fallback. Preserve dimensions and alpha from decode.
files: crates/buzz-scene/src/image.rs (only if ImageFill lacks a matrix field)
steps.verification: New fixture test: XFL with an embedded PNG bitmap fill asserts the resulting object's Paint::image() resolves to the asset and pixel data matches; existing grey-fallback tests updated.

steps.description: Give text/video/sound explicit placeholders (plan step 3 'explicit placeholders where conversion is incomplete'): DOMStaticText/DynamicText/InputText -> placeholder shape sized from the XFL bounds with a report entry naming the frame/layer; DOMVideoInstance and DOMSoundItem keep their current unsupported entries but attach location info. No silent drops.
steps.verification: cargo test -p buzz-import-xfl: extend unsupported_features_are_reported to assert placeholders exist for text and that report issues include the element name.

steps.description: Run full verification: cargo test -p buzz-import-xfl && cargo test -p buzz-doc (serialization of imported scenes) and build the app. If a real failing FLA is available, import it and compare inventory counts before/after.
steps.verification: All listed suites pass; import report on the fixture shows zero unexplained omissions for supported constructs.

risks: Working tree has ~150 dirty files from interrupted work — new changes must not clobber unrelated edits.
XFL fill-matrix semantics (registration point vs. transform) are easy to get subtly wrong; need an Animate-authored fixture or careful derivation, image similarity alone won't prove it.
No licensed Adobe Animate available for round-trip validation per the plan's own caveat — mark Adobe-side checks unavailable.
questions: Do you have a representative failing .fla/.xfl file to use as the regression fixture (plan §4 requires one)?
Priority check: bitmap fills first, or should text rendering come before them this round?
